meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and did anyone speak to him first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. He writes it somewhere else and pastes it in, Hale. And you still haven't said whether anyone spoke to Owen before November 3.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine, it stands for now. Whatever happens next stays off his record and stays out of his classroom. And for the third time, was Owen heard before the zero went in?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Editions differ. Which one is that, and is it the one your class uses?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Usually. You've skipped the edition the same way you've skipped whether Owen was heard first.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Outlines change, that's what they're for. You're putting a lot in front of me, and you still won't answer a simple procedural question.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, and Owen does the rewrite to put this behind him, nothing more. Tonight, in writing, with the date fixed before December 1 and the zero coming off when the mark goes in. And I still want an answer on whether anyone spoke to him before you entered it.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
He works after school some days, so I'll confirm Thursday when I answer your email tonight. Who supervises it?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school and not in front of Owen's class, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require the name of the person supervising the rewrite and a direct answer on whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero was entered. I expect that in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite under 4.4 before December 1. She still wants it in writing tonight, the supervisor named, and an answer on whether Owen was heard first, and that is the fair outcome.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and answered her pasted-from-elsewhere defence by offering to look at any dated draft, which gave her something she could check and couldn't argue past.
What cost ground: You never answered whether Owen was spoken to before the zero went in, even though she asked several times, so she kept a procedural grievance open all the way through.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, which came very close to that night. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after your opening apology, when she asked whether Owen was heard first, give her a straight yes or no so she has nothing procedural left to hold against you.
